label: theorem: Murasugi sum multiplicativity of ADO
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem: Murasugi sum multiplicativity of ADO}
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple complex Lie algebra of type ADE and $r\geq 3$. If $L$ is a Murasugi sum of $L_1$ and $L_2$ along connected minimal genus Seifert surfaces, then $$\text{top}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)=\text{top}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L_1)\cdot \text{top}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L_2).$$

title: Theorem
body_md:
(Gabai)
    Let $\Sigma$ be a Murasugi sum of $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$. Then $\Sigma$ is a genus-minimizing Seifert surface for the link $L=\partial\Sigma$ if and only if each $\Sigma_i$ is a genus-minimizing Seifert surface for $L_i=\partial\Sigma_i$, $i=1,2$.
head: environment

title: Notation
body_md:
In what follows, $\mathfrak{g}$ denotes a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra of rank $n$, $\mathfrak{h}$ a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak{g}$, $\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\}$ a set of positive simple roots, $(a_{ij})$ its Cartan matrix and $\Delta^+$ the set of positive roots. We work in the type ADE case only, so $(a_{ij})$ is symmetric. We define $H_1,\dots,H_n\in \mathfrak{h}$ by $\alpha_i(H_j)=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$. We let $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij}$ and extend it to a form $(-,-)$ on $\mathfrak{h}^*$ so that $(\lambda,\alpha_i)=\lambda(H_i)$ for all $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathfrak{h}^*$. We denote by $L_R, L_W\subset \mathfrak{h}^*$ the root and weight lattices of $\mathfrak{g}$ respectively. We denote $\rho=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\beta\in\Delta^+}\beta\in L_W$. We also denote by $L_R^+$ the set of positive vectors in $L_R$ i.e. those vectors $\sum_{i=1}^nk_i\alpha_i$ with all $k_i\geq 0$ and some $k_j>0$ and for any $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in L_R$ we write $\gamma_1> \gamma_2$ if $\gamma_1-\gamma_2\in L_R^+.$ \\

Let $q$ be a primitive root of unity of order $r$, say $q=e^{\frac{2\pi i}{r}}$, and for every $z\in \mathbb{C}$ set $q^z=e^{\frac{2\pi i z}{r}}$ and $[z]_{q}=\frac{q^z-q^{-z}}{q-q^{-1}}$. For $k\in\mathbb{N}$ denote $[k]_q!=[k]_q[k-1]_q\cdots [1]_q$. Let $r'=r$ if $r$ is odd and $r'=r/2$ if $r$ is even.  \\

For any $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\in\mathfrak{h}^*$ we let $\lambda_i=\lambda(H_i)$. The reader can assume that $\lambda_i\in \mathbb{C}\setminus \mathbb{Z}$ for every $i$, though $\lambda$ typical is enough. As mentioned above, we set $t_i=q^{2\lambda_i}$ and $\boldsymbol{t}^{\alpha}=t_1^{a_1}\dots t_n^{a_n}$ for any $\alpha=\sum a_i\alpha_i\in L_R$. With this notation we have $q^{(r'-1)(\lambda,2\rho)}=\boldsymbol{t}^{(r'-1)\rho}$.\\


Some proofs use graphical notation. We use the convention that diagrams are read from bottom to top, so an arrow colored by $V$ represents $\text{id}_V$ (resp. $\text{id}_{V^*}$) if oriented upwards (resp. downwards).

body_md: The set $$\{K_{\alpha}F^IE^J \ | \ \alpha\in Q_r \text{ and } I,J:\Delta^+\to\{0,\dots,r'-1\}\}$$ forms a basis of $\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$.

title: Remark
body_md: The group $G$ is isomorphic to a torus $(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^n$ where $n=\text{rank}(\mathfrak{g})$. Thus, we like to call $\mathcal{C}^H_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ a {\em toric tensor category}. Though we do not explicitly use it, this torus grading is essential for our results and is the main difference with quantum groups (of Lie algebras) at generic $q$. It is very interesting to note that, for some quantized Lie superalgebras, the toric structure is present even when $q$ is generic. This is the case for the ``type I'' Lie superalgebras (except $\mathfrak{psl}(n|n)$), and its the reason why analogous results can be expected for them (see \cite{GLN:genus-for-Lie-superalgebras} for genus bounds).

label: lemma: coeffs of iota X
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: coeffs of iota X}
    If $\boldsymbol{\lambda}\equiv \lambda$ is diagonal, then $\iota_X$ has coefficients in $t^{(r'-1)(\rho,\rho)}\mathbb{Q}(q)$ in the standard bases of $X^*$ and $X$ (here $t=q^{2\lambda}$).
head: environment

label: lemma: coev lemma
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Indeed
    \begin{align*}
    (\iota_X\otimes (\overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}&\circ\overrightarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}))\circ\overrightarrow{\text{coev}}_X(1)\\
    &=\sum_{I,J} q^{(r'-1)(2\rho, d(J)-d(I))}\iota_X(v_I\otimes v_J')'\otimes (\overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\circ\overrightarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}})(v_I\otimes v'_J)\\
     &=\sum_{I,J,C} q^{(r'-1)[(2\rho, d(J)-d(I))+(2\rho,\boldsymbol{\lambda}-d(J))]}v_J\otimes v'_I\otimes \delta_{I,J}q^{(1-r')(2\rho,\boldsymbol{\lambda}-d(I))}v_C\otimes v'_C\\
     &=\sum_{I,C}v_I\otimes v'_I\otimes v_C\otimes v'_C\\
     &=\overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\otimes \overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}.
    \end{align*}

label: lemma: braiding on cXX expressed as R-matrix on some small uqgL
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: braiding on cXX expressed as R-matrix on some small uqgL}
For each $\mathfrak{g}$ of type ADE and $r\geq 3$ there is a lattice $L$ (that depends on $r$) with $L_R\subset L\subset L_W$ having the following property:
there exists $\overline{\mathcal{K}}_L\in \mathbb{Q}(q)[L]^{\otimes 2}$ such that for every $V,W\in \mathcal{C}^H_{[0]}$ the braiding $c_{V,W}$ coincides with left multiplication by $\overline{\mathcal{K}}_L\cdot \overline{\Theta}$, where $\overline{\Theta}\in \mathfrak{u}_q^{L}(\mathfrak{g})^{\otimes 2}$ is as before: $$c_{V,W}(v\otimes w)=\tau_{V,W}(\overline{\mathcal{K}}_L\cdot\overline{\Theta}(v\otimes w)).$$ 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
Moreover, when $(r,\det(A))=1$ one can take $L=L_R$ and $\overline{\mathcal{K}}\cdot \overline{\Theta}$ to be the $R$-matrix of $\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$. When $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $r$ is even one can take $L=L_W$ and $\overline{\mathcal{K}}\cdot\overline{\Theta}$ the $R$-matrix of $\mathfrak{u}^{L_W}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of \cite{FGST:modular, BBGe:logarithmic}.

title: Proposition
body_md: $ADO_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ is insensitive to reversing the orientation of all components of $L$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $\overline{L}$ be the link $L$ with the orientation reversed on all components. As usual, we have $F(\overline{L}_o, V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})=F(L_o, V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^*)$. But $V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^*\cong \omega(V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})$ as mentioned above. Now, rotating a braid by 180 degress around a vertical axis does not change any invariant. But it clearly exchanges the $E$'s with $F's$ on all crossings, and the pivots $g$ to $g^{-1}$'s, hence it is the same as applying $\omega$. This shows that $F(L_o,\omega(V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}))=F(L_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})$, hence $F(\overline{L}_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})=F(L_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})$ from which $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(\overline{L})=\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ follows.
head: environment

label: prop: symmetry of ADO
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The modules $V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^*$ and $V_{-\boldsymbol{\lambda}+(r'-1)2\rho}$ have the same character, so they are isomorphic for typical $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ \cite{GP:trace-projective-quantum-groups, Rupert:unrolled}. Thus, we have $$F(L_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})=F(\overline{L}_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}})=F(L_o,V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^*)=F(L_o,V_{-\boldsymbol{\lambda}+(r'-1)2\rho})$$ where the first equality follows from the previous proposition. This proves the first statement. Now, it is well-known that $2\rho(H_i)=(2\rho,\alpha_i)=(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)$ and this is equal to 2 for every $i$ in the simply-laced case. Thus, the right hand side is $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ with variables specialized to $q^{-\lambda_i+(r'-1)2\rho(H_i)}=q^{-\lambda_i-2}$ for every $i$ (here $\lambda_i=\boldsymbol{\lambda}(H_i)$), that is $$\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(q^{\lambda_1},\dots, q^{\lambda_n})=\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(q^{-\lambda_1-2},\dots, q^{-\lambda_n-2})$$
   from which the result follows.
head: environment

label: prop: top of ADOgr is top of Pgr
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: top of ADOgr is top of Pgr}
    The coefficient of $\boldsymbol{t}^{(r'-1)\rho \cdot (2g(L)+s-1)}$ in $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ is the same as the coefficient of $t^{(r'-1)(\rho,\rho)(2g(L)+s-1)}$ in $P_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$.
head: environment
labels: prop: top of ADOgr is top of Pgr

title: Proof
body_md: This is simply because $\alpha<\beta$ in $\frac{1}{2}L_R$ implies $(\alpha,\rho)<(\beta,\rho)$. Since the $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ bound holds for the $L_R$-degree, the only term of $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ that contributes to $t^{(r'-1)(\rho,\rho)(2g(L)+s-1)}$ after specialization is the term in degree $\boldsymbol{t}^{(r'-1)\rho(2g(L)+s-1)}$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
In type ADE, the least coefficient of $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ (or $P_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$) is related to the top coefficient by
$$\text{least}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)=\text{top}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)\cdot q^{(2g(L)+s-1)(2\rho,2\rho)}.$$

body_md: The vector $v_I\otimes v'_J$ has weight $-d(I)+d(J)$ so $E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v'_J)$ has weight $-d(I)+d(J)+d(I_{max})$. Since $-a_i+b_i>0$, the $\alpha_i$-component of this vector is greater than that of $d(I_{max})$. label: lemma: commuting F^I with E^I
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Obviously true for $f=F_i,e=E_j$. Using that $$[ff',e]=f[f',e]+[f,e]f'$$
    it follows by induction that $[f,E_j]$ is in $U^{\leq 0}$ for all $f\in U^-$. Similarly, using that $$[f,ee']=[f,e]e'+e[f,e']$$
    an another induction (in which the previous case is the base case), the lemma follows.

title: Lemma
body_md: If $d(I)\neq d(J)$, then $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v'_J)$ is a vector of $X$ for which, when expressed in the standard basis, all coefficients are polynomials in $t^{-1}$ of degree $<(r'-1)(2\rho,\rho)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If for some $i$, the $\alpha_i$-component of $d(I)$ is $<$ than that of $d(J)$, then $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v'_J)=0$ by the first part of the previous lemma. If on the other hand, some $\alpha_i$-component of $d(I)$ is $>$ than that of $d(J)$, then one can commute $$F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}=E^{I_{max}}F^{I_{max}}+\sum_{A,B,C}c_{A,B,C}K^AF^BE^C$$
    with $d(B),d(C)<d(I_{max})$ and $c_{A,B,C}\in \mathbb{Q}(q)$ by Lemma \ref{lemma: commuting F^I with E^I}. But then $$F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v'_J)=\sum_{A,B,C}c_{A,B,C}K^AF^BE^C(v_I\otimes v'_J)$$
    by the second part of the previous lemma. Finally, since $d(C)<d(I_{max})=(r'-1)2\rho$ for each $C$ on the RHS, we get the desired result by Proposition \ref{lemma: algebraic bounds}.

body_md:
Let $B:X	o X$ be the action of $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}-\Lambda$, we will check that $B(v_I\otimes v'_J)$ has coefficients of the desired degree. Indeed, if $d(I)
eq d(J)$, $F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v'_J)$ has coefficients of the desired degree by the previous lemma while $\Lambda(v_I\otimes v'_J)=0$ if $I
eq J$ (in particular if $d(I)
eq d(J)$) by Lemma ef{lemma: CGPT's lemma for cointegral}, hence the same holds for $B(v_I\otimes v'_J)$. On the other hand, $ rac{1}{|G|}\sum_AK^A$ acts as the identity on weight zero vectors, hence if $d(I)=d(J)$ one has $$\Lambda(v_I\otimes v_J)=F^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}(v_I\otimes v_J)$$

label: prop: Seifert formula
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Seifert formula}
    If $\Sigma$ is a connected Seifert surface of a link $L$ built from an $N$-component tangle $T_{\Sigma}$ as above, then the $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ invariant of $L$ is determined by $T_{\Sigma}$ as
    $$\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)\cdot\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}=(\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\otimes \overleftarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}^{\otimes 2N})\circ(\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma},X)\otimes\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}})$$
    where $\overline{F}(T_{\Sigma},X)=\mathcal{J}_X\circ F(T_{\Sigma},X)$ is determined by left multiplication of the universal invariant $Z'_T$ acting on $X^{\otimes N}$ as in (\ref{eq: RT of T in terms of universal}).

label: remark: scalar ovmu on ribbon v
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark: scalar ovmu on ribbon v}
If the cointegral of $\mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{g})$ used is $\Lambda=\Lambda_GF^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}}$ and $\mu$ is such that $\mu(\Lambda)=1$ then the scalar $\overline{\mu}(v)$ can be explicitly computed as $$\overline{\mu}(v)=\left(\frac{q^{1-r'}}{r'}(q-q^{-1})^{2(r'-1)}\right)^{|\Delta_+|}\cdot q^{-2(2\rho,2\rho)}.$$
    Indeed, by the formula of the $R$-matrix the ribbon element can be computed to be $$v=\sum_Iq^{-(d(I),d(I))}c_IF^IK_{2\rho}^{1-r'}E^I.$$
    Noting that after applying $\overline{\mu}$ only the term with $I=I_{max}$ survives, using $d(I_{max})=(r'-1)2\rho$ and commuting $F^{I_{max}}K_{2\rho}^{1-r'}=q^{-(r'-1)^2(2\rho,2\rho)}K_{2\rho}^{1-r'}F^{I_{max}}$ and using $\Lambda_GK_{2\rho}^{1-r'}=\Lambda_G$ gives $$\overline{\mu}(v)=q^{-2(r'-1)^2(2\rho,2\rho)}c_{I_{max}}\mu(\Lambda_GF^{I_{max}}E^{I_{max}})=q^{-2(2\rho,2\rho)}c_{I_{max}}.$$
    Plugging in (\ref{eq: formula for cImax}) we get the desired formula.

label: lemma: B has smaller deg after closing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: B has smaller deg after closing}
  The operators $$\text{cl}(B):=(\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\otimes\overleftarrow{\text{ev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}^{\otimes 2N})\circ (B\otimes \text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}):V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}\to V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$$
  and
  $$\text{cl}(B'):= (\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\otimes B' )\circ (\overleftarrow{\text{coev}}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}^{\otimes 2N'}\otimes \text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}):V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}\to V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$$
  have coefficients which are Laurent polynomials in $t$ satisfying $\text{max-deg}_{t^{\pm 1}}<(r'-1)(\rho,\rho) \cdot N$ and $\text{max-deg}_{t^{\pm 1}}< (r'-1)(\rho,\rho)\cdot N'$ respectively.
head: environment
labels: lemma: B has smaller deg after closing

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the previous proof, after closing strands we get
$$\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)\cdot\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}-(\kappa(\lambda)^N\overline{\mu}^{\otimes N}(Z_T))\cdot\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}=(\text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}\otimes \overleftarrow{\text{ev}}^{\otimes 2N})\circ(B\otimes \text{id}_{V_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}).$$
As before, the least term of $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ coincides with that of $(\kappa(\lambda)^N\overline{\mu}^{\otimes N}(Z_T)$. But since $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}$ and $\kappa(\lambda)$ satisfy the same symmetry (and $\overline{\mu}^{\otimes N}(Z_T)\in\mathbb{Q}(q)$) by Lemma \ref{lemma: symmetry of kappa} and Proposition \ref{prop: symmetry of ADO}, it follows that they also have the same top term. This implies that the RHS cannot have a non-trivial coefficient in degree $(r'-1)(\rho,\rho)\cdot N$, as desired. The same argument applies to $\text{cl}(B')$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The above lemma would not have been necessary if the tensor $B$ had coefficients satisfying $\text{max-deg}_{t^{-1}}<(r'-1)(\rho,\rho) \cdot N$ and $\text{max-deg}_{t}< (r'-1)(\rho,\rho)\cdot N$, but we could only prove $\leq$ in the last inequality.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: If $L$ is a Murasugi-sum of links $L_1,L_2$ along connected minimal genus Seifert surfaces, then the genus bound for $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L)$ of \cite{LNV:genus-unrolled} is sharp iff it is sharp for both $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L_1)$ and  $\text{ADO}_{\mathfrak{g},r}(L_2)$.
